title: ClayCode CC7 Scoped Transition Closure
summary: CC7 refines CC6/G6 into an OPEN CC-RC1.2 Transition Closure Capsule: the global root identifies the basis snapshot; trusted operation semantics derive dependency/effect/capability closure; commit-time freshness checks relevant versions/invariant epochs and escalates conservatively for unknown effects. Wire/projection identity remains separate from semantic identity.
key_deltas: global state root is snapshot identity, not necessarily sole commit freshness predicate
trusted op semantics derive read/write/invariant/effect/capability requirements
unknown/dynamic effects escalate to broader closure
semantic hashes are independent from incidental wire serialization
Qwen3-4B projection factorial remains blocked by provider inference-credit exhaustion
open_questions: Can a real Clay/FRANK operation registry derive conservative useful dependency/effect closures?
What granularity of object version and invariant epoch minimizes retries without excessive metadata?
When should scoped validation escalate to whole-root or coordinated closure?
Does Qwen3-4B read compact ClayCode more accurately per token than positional JSON?
Should cryptographic/Merkle witnesses be used only across trust boundaries or also for local replay/audit?
highest_information_next_test: Implement 10-20 pinned ClayCode operations with deterministic footprint derivation, instrument their dynamic access traces, then benchmark whole-root vs scoped validation under realistic concurrent state churn; separately rerun the pinned Qwen3-4B reader factorial when model inference quota is available.
